This vignette shows how to compile a spreadsheet-style pipeline into the
canonical YAML form and then reuse that written YAML with the normal `tsflow`
workflow.

The pattern is:

- read a CSV pipeline and its sidecar
- write the parsed pipeline to YAML
- plan from the written YAML
- execute from the written YAML

## Start From CSV

This vignette uses a small temporary CSV pipeline together with a sibling
sidecar.

```{r}
library(tsflow)

dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)

csv_path <- file.path(dir, "pipeline.csv")
meta_path <- file.path(dir, "pipeline.meta.yml")

writeLines(
    c(
        "name,input,step_1",
        "derived_a,raw_a,\"scale(@factor)\""
    ),
    con = csv_path
)
writeLines(
    c(
        "vars:",
        "  factor: 100",
        "outputs:",
        "  - derived_a"
    ),
    con = meta_path
)

cat(paste(readLines(csv_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

```{r}
cat(paste(readLines(meta_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

`read_pipeline()` merges the CSV and sidecar into one in-memory pipeline object.

```{r}
parsed <- read_pipeline(csv_path)

names(parsed)
parsed$vars
head(vapply(parsed$series, `[[`, character(1), "name"))
```

## Write Canonical YAML

You can persist that parsed pipeline to disk with `write_pipeline()`.

```{r}
yaml_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
write_pipeline(parsed, yaml_path)

cat(paste(readLines(yaml_path), collapse = "\n"))
```

The written file is ordinary pipeline YAML, so it can be read again directly:

```{r}
reparsed <- read_pipeline(yaml_path)
identical(reparsed, parsed)
```

## Plan From The Written YAML

Planning works the same way as with the original CSV. The only difference is
that the compiled YAML now contains the merged pipeline definition in one file.

```{r}
scale <- function(x, factor) {
    x * factor
}

plan <- plan_pipeline(yaml_path, transform_env = environment())

plan
head(plan$dag$order)
```

## Execute From The Written YAML

Execution also uses the same API. Once the YAML is written, it is just another
pipeline definition file.

```{r}
inputs <- list(raw_a = stats::ts(c(1, 2, 3, 4), start = c(2020, 1), frequency = 4))

result <- execute_pipeline(
    path = yaml_path,
    inputs = inputs,
    transform_env = environment()
)

result$outputs$derived_a
```

## When This Is Useful

Writing the parsed YAML is useful when you want to:

- inspect the exact pipeline that `read_pipeline()` produced
- diff compiled pipeline output in git
- debug CSV translation issues
- keep one canonical pipeline artifact on disk for later planning and execution
